appstore.name: Flagship
appstore.subtitle: Your cloud, on your hardware
appstore.promotionalText: New in 0.3: your phone checks every new server is really yours, AI runs on your own server, and the app speaks seven languages. Still free.
appstore.description:
Flagship turns a spare computer into your own cloud. Your phone holds the keys.

Your apps, files and backups live on a server you own: an old PC, a mini PC, or a virtual machine on a computer you already use. Each server gets its own web address with a real green padlock, and the encryption ends on your server, not on ours. Flagship can't read what your apps send.

WHAT YOU CAN DO
• Set up a server in about ten minutes with Flagship Studio on your computer.
• Approve your server's start with Face ID, or let it start on its own if you choose.
• Build apps by describing them, or install them from a git repository.
• Invite family and friends to one app at a time. They get that app, never your keys.
• Back up your servers to your phone or to your other servers. Only your account can open the backups.
• Run AI models on your own server. Your prompts and data stay there.
• See your servers on Apple Watch, and approve a start from your wrist.

NEW IN 0.3
• The first time you approve a new server, your phone keeps that server's own key and checks it every time after. It shows a six-digit code to compare with the server's screen.
• Your own page at voi.ci/your-name: a photo, a short bio, your links and posts. People with a Flagship account can send you messages from it, end-to-end encrypted. They appear as visitors, never by name.
• Local AI: download a model to your server and use it in your apps and builds. Nothing is sent anywhere.
• Apps get their own database, can be made of several parts, and can be small WebAssembly programs.
• An app that needs a graphics card waits for your approval.
• Choose for each app whether updates wait for you, wait a week, or install at once.
• Server updates prove they are healthy, or step back on their own.
• The server software was rebuilt for security: it no longer runs as root, keeps its keys in a separate service, and installs only signed packages.
• If flagshipserver.com can't be reached, your phone can still find your server on your home Wi-Fi, show its status, start and stop apps, and make a backup.
• Choose how long each server keeps serving its apps if no admin opens Flagship: 7 days, 30 days or no time limit.
• Check that your server runs the official Node.js from nodejs.org, against a list Flagship signs.
• English, Spanish, French, German, Brazilian Portuguese, Japanese and Simplified Chinese.

PRIVACY, PLAINLY
• Encryption ends on your server. Our relay passes the encrypted traffic along and sees connection metadata: which server, when, and how much.
• No email, no password, no phone number. Your account is a set of keys on your devices.
• An AI model never learns who or where you are.
• The code is public at github.com/ibisllc/flagship.

Flagship is free. There is nothing to buy.

You need a server: a spare computer, or a computer that runs Flagship Studio (macOS and Windows; Linux is experimental).
appstore.whatsNew:
Flagship 0.3 is our biggest update yet.

• Your phone keeps each new server's own key the first time you approve it, and shows a six-digit code to compare with the server's screen. Studio checks the code for you when it hosts the server.
• Your own page at voi.ci/your-name, made in the new Messages tab. People with a Flagship account can write to you from it. Messages are end-to-end encrypted, and senders appear as visitors, never by name. Block and Report are one tap away.
• Local AI: download a model to your server from its page. Your apps and builds can use it, and nothing is sent anywhere.
• Apps get their own database, can be made of several parts, and can be WebAssembly programs.
• Apps that need a graphics card wait for your approval.
• Choose for each app: updates wait for you, wait a week, or install at once.
• Before an AI repair spends your key or credits, you see the cost and agree.
• Apps can ask to talk to other people's apps. You choose Allow, Always allow or Deny.
• Approve a server's start from Apple Watch, even with your iPhone locked.
• If flagshipserver.com can't be reached, your phone can still find your server on your home Wi-Fi, show its status, start and stop apps, and make a backup.
• Server updates prove they are healthy, or go back on their own.
• The server no longer runs as root, keeps its keys in a separate service, and installs only signed packages.
• Recovery now checks your passkey as well as your passphrase.
• Choose how long each server keeps serving its apps if no admin opens Flagship: 7 days, 30 days or no time limit.
• Each server's page has a Runtime card that checks it runs the official Node.js.
• Rescue my data, in Settings, saves a backup of your server to your phone over your home Wi-Fi.
• Anyone can report a voi.ci link or an app at flagshipserver.com/abuse. Owners get a notice with a deadline before any suspension, except for the most serious abuse.
• Our relay was rewritten in Rust: it needs much less memory and lets us add more relays later.
• Coming from 0.2? Update each server too: its page tells you when it needs it.
• Account names and voi.ci link names are 3 to 30 characters.
• New languages: Spanish, French, German, Brazilian Portuguese, Japanese and Simplified Chinese.
• Redesigned Home, Activity and Settings.
